data.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:122-176` searches Dockerfile text, so a later broken final stage can still pass. `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1944-1972` and `test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:97-101` accept commands that merely contain loopback health tokens without opening a socket.

## Approach

Parse the shipped final Docker stage and inspect its effective entrypoint, installed artifacts, and health command. Execute the configured health command against controlled good and bad listeners so the oracle observes a real socket and response. Keep this in the portable Python test path; do not require Docker.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`
- `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp`
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`

## Testing

Add a broken trailing-stage fixture, a no-op URL-print command, a healthy listener, and malformed/closed-listener controls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A broken shipped final stage fails even when an earlier stage retains all expected tokens.
- [ ] A command that only prints the health URL fails the oracle.
- [ ] The real configured health command succeeds against a valid listener and fails on closed or malformed response paths.
- [ ] The focused tests run without Docker and leave normal local/default test dependencies unchanged.
data.title: Parse shipped container stages and prove live health-command semantics
